stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // F10 LIGHTRUNNER

//Skydio

📍San Mateo, CA

Tech: Autonomous long-range flight

Platform: Fixed-wing aircraft

Goal: Give responders a live aerial view over long distances, where quadcopters cannot reach fast enough.

Why: Skydio says a single MegaDock with F10's 30-mile flight radius covers nearly 3,000 square miles from one launch location.

Private company → Backers: Not stated in source.

Traction: In development, with customer deployment planned for 2027, per Skydio.

Skydio's F10 Lightrunner is its first fixed-wing aircraft, built for emergency response, search and rescue, and asset inspection missions that span miles. Skydio says it can launch itself, cover ground at highway speed and stream live video while ground units are still on the road. A robotic takeoff and landing system and the MegaDock, which houses up to five F10s, are meant to remove the need for ground crew to run it.

Skydio also announced Asset Command and Security Command, software platforms for drone inspections and physical security, both available to purchase now with general availability early next year. Skydio says F10 deploys to customers in 2027.

Source: Skydio, Inc., Sept. 24, 2026

Image: skydio.com (courtesy)

fields.headline: PARAVISION WINS UP TO $6.5M STATE DEAL
fields.deck: The award covers digital identity assurance, with $1.3 million obligated at signing.

stories.caption:
Paravision, a facial recognition developer, has won a State Department contract worth up to $6.5 million. Federal procurement records describe the work as "digital detection/identity assurance." The award was made September 23 and runs through September 22, 2031. The firm-fixed-price deal began with $1.3 million obligated.

The department competed the award under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside and received a single offer. Public records do not name the Paravision products bought. The description lines up with the company's deepfake detection tools, which flag manipulated and AI-generated faces, but the record does not show whether the award includes deepfake detection, liveness detection, facial recognition or other software.

The September award is far larger than an earlier April 30 State Department purchase order to Paravision for $24,717, listed as a "purchase card for software license." Records do not show whether that purchase was a test, a pilot or a step toward the September award.

Source: Biometric Update, October 17, 2026

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel entry, in the Gulf of America.

Why: Vessels operate without a crew aboard, so surveillance can continue in conditions where crewed patrols would be impractical.

Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Lightfish vessels operating on the Rio Grande since January 2026 in support of federal border security efforts, per Seasats. Fleet deployed in the Gulf of America, per Seasats.

Seasats said a fleet of Lightfish unmanned surface vessels has now been placed in service for U.S. maritime border security in the Gulf, extending an autonomous surveillance effort that already runs with federal homeland defense backing. The vessels launch from the Texas coast and conduct persistent surveillance in the Gulf.

Each Lightfish is about 11 feet long and weighs 340 pounds. The vessels are solar powered and can stay on station for multi-month periods. Seasats says two people can launch and recover one from a boat ramp or a pickup truck. The deployment follows Operation River Wall on the southern border.

Seasats said offshore patrols by manned aircraft and boats are limited by crew endurance, operating cost and coverage area. The company described the fleet as a way to extend continuous coverage alongside existing assets.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, Oct. 2, 2026

Image: prnewswire.com (courtesy)

fields.headline: XTEND SECURES 6,000 STRIKER SYSTEMS
fields.deck: The company says the order follows its Gauntlet II top-performer selection.

frames.mediaQuery: XTEND STRIKER drone close quarters battle

stories.caption:
XTEND AI Robotics (NYSE: XTND) reports an award worth $40.5 million for 6,000 STRIKER systems. The business was named a top performer in the Close Quarters Battle segment of Gauntlet II, part of the U.S. Department of War's Drone Dominance Program, an iterative program valued at $1 billion.

STRIKER runs on XTEND's proprietary XOS operating system and is built for tactical missions in confined, complex and GNSS-denied settings. CEO Aviv Shapira said, "We competed, we proved our capabilities, and now we are ready to build."

Gauntlet II top performers move straight to Gauntlet III in the same segment of Phase 3, which opened September 28, 2026, but only after completing a 400-system production order. The company says Gauntlet III results will decide whether any Phase 3 orders are placed, and that taking part does not guarantee an award. XTEND also gave preliminary third quarter 2026 revenue and a backlog update.

Source: XTEND AI Robotics, Inc. via Business Wire, Oct. 13, 2026

fields.headline: ARMY TO TEST COUNTER-DRONE TECH IN AFRICA
fields.deck: The effort aims to deliver field-ready systems to Soldiers within 180 days.

frames.mediaQuery: Army counter-drone or African Lion 26 autonomous systems, public domain U.S. Army imagery

stories.caption:
SETAF-AF, the Army's southern European task force in Africa, is teaming with the Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate, or G-TEAD, to try out new systems on the continent and get proven ones to units quickly.

The first accelerated capability event, or ACE, is set for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. It will target counter-unmanned aircraft systems and force protection, with a focus on shielding early-entry command posts and operating locations from Group 1–3 small UAS. Army officials say Africa's open airspace and varied terrain give Soldiers conditions that U.S. and European training ranges cannot easily match.

Each ACE runs in three phases: submission and preparation, Soldier-led demonstrations, and follow-on operational evaluation. The next steps are a Soldier-led demonstration in February and March 2027, then an operational assessment in April and May during African Lion 2027. G-TEAD plans to validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires as the transition partner.

Source: U.S. Army, Oct. 16, 2026

fields.headline: OSC OFFERS ANTHEIA UP TO $80M LOAN
fields.deck: The conditional loan would support Antheia's U.S. drug ingredient manufacturing.

stories.caption:
The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital has issued a conditional commitment for a direct, long-term loan of up to $80 million to Antheia, a biosynthesis company based in Menlo Park, California. The financing, combined with additional private capital, would support Antheia's plan to onshore production of critical pharmaceutical ingredients.

Roughly 90 percent of the U.S. supply of key starting materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients comes from foreign countries, according to the company. Antheia argues that this reliance exposes Americans to drug shortages when public health emergencies, natural disasters, geopolitical tensions or supply chain failures disrupt those sources.

The commitment is conditional. Antheia must complete additional steps before financial close, including meeting financial, legal, technical, investment and due diligence requirements. The company has previously received $32 million in non-dilutive federal financing and equity from strategic government-affiliated investors.

Dr. Christina Smolke, CEO and co-founder of Antheia, said: "Advanced biomanufacturing offers the U.S. a direct path to securing these supply chains while regaining global leadership in a strategic technology sector."

Source: PR Newswire, Oct. 18, 2026
